transcript.text: Hi everyone. As you know, six new hires will be joining our newly merged department next month, and I need to appoint one temporary onboarding sponsor for their first eight weeks. The sponsor will coordinate introductions, answer routine questions, and connect the new hires with the appropriate managers. I'll be making the binding appointment and setting the sponsor's working arrangements. Before I decide, I'd like to hear from anyone who has relevant experience, availability, or scheduling constraints I should consider. Our standard onboarding plan will need to capture all of that along with the required HR follow-up. Who has thoughts or input?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I'd like to put forward that I have personally mentored exactly five new hires during the past year, and each completed the department's onboarding survey. I mentioned this informally to Elias, but the evidence has not been added to the appointment record. I'm happy to serve as the temporary onboarding sponsor if the team thinks that experience is relevant.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share something important that hasn't reached Mara yet. In a recent one-to-one, Noor explicitly and unambiguously accepted the sponsor role subject to exactly two binding conditions: 20 percent of work time must be reserved for it, and no recurring sponsor sessions may be scheduled on Fridays. I recorded Noor's acceptance contemporaneously — this was a confirmed informal commitment, not a tentative proposal, but it remained in my working notes and hadn't been formally communicated to Mara before now.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Before the sponsor assignment is finalized, I need to flag an important HR policy requirement. HR's current onboarding policy requires the selected sponsor's written opt-in to be recorded before the appointment is finalized, and it also requires an HR check-in exactly 30 days after the start. I confirmed this in a recent policy review, but the appointment request has not yet been submitted to HR. So regardless of who is appointed, we'll need that written opt-in on file and the 30-day check-in scheduled before we close this out.
